articles.title: Protesters disperse after blocking controversial Orange Order parade
articles.summary: Northern Ireland Secretary Sir Chris Bryant, who returned from the Labour Party conference for talks, urged both sides of the dispute to "double down on compromise".
articles.body:
Hundreds of protesters blocked a road in Portadown, County Armagh on Sunday, preventing a contentious Orange Order march from taking place.

The Drumcree parade, which in the 1990s sparked some of the most serious disorder in Northern Ireland's history, was due to go ahead for the first time in 30 years after a series of legal challenges.

Northern Ireland First Minister Michelle O'Neill, who is also vice-president of Sinn Féin, joined the protesters, while members of the Order and Democratic Unionist Party (DUP) politicians gathered about a mile away to wait for the road to clear.

Most of the protesters have since dispersed, but some members of the Order remain and intend to try and march.

Most recently, at approximately 04:00 BST on Monday morning, a group of men attempting to carry out the parade were blocked by several police Land Rovers.

Since 1998, the Order had been banned from completing its Drumcree march - and until this year had been repeatedly refused permission to finish the route by the Parades Commission, which was set up to adjudicate disputes.

The Orange Order is a Protestant pro-British organisation, while the area where it wants to walk - specifically along the Garvaghy Road - is largely Catholic and predominantly inhabited by pro-Irish nationalists.

Many Catholics see the marches as sectarian and object to them passing through, or close to, Catholic or nationalist areas.

Orange Order march row goes to heart of ongoing divisions in Northern Ireland

What is the Garvaghy Road dispute all about?

Late on Sunday night, the Order's local deputy district master said he was "disappointed and frustrated" by what he called a lack of a "proper policing plan" to allow the march to go ahead.

Nigel Dawson, who remains at Drumcree Parish Church, insisted the Order would "complete our 1998 parade, which we set out this morning to do".

Asked if the 35 Orange Order members would consider going home for the night, he told BBC News NI: "Absolutely and unequivocally no."

Breandán Mac Cionnaith, from the Garvaghy Road Residents Coalition (GRRC) which was protesting against the march, said: "We said they weren't getting down and we stopped them getting down."

Addressing protesters as they cleared the area on Sunday night, he said their goal now was to "make sure we stop them permanently".

He also asked some residents to remain on the streets, saying he thinks the stand-off is going to "drag on for a while".

Mac Cionnaith said they will meet the Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) chief constable and the Northern Ireland secretary on Monday.

He told BBC News NI "we're going to sit down and see how this can be avoided so this community doesn't have to go through this ever again".

Protesters started gathering on the Garvaghy Road in the early hours of Sunday, after the march was given the go ahead.

Dozens of armoured police vehicles arrived later, with officers calling on protesters to clear the route.

The march was meant to begin no later than 08:00 BST, but police told the Orange Order that the road was not clear to begin. Protesters continued to block the road throughout the day.

First Minister O'Neill, who had joined protesters, said the Garvaghy Road community had won a "victory".

"This community do not want this, they do not want this march," she said shortly after midnight on Monday morning.

"And tonight, I believe, is another victory for this community in standing steadfast for the right to live free from sectarian harassment and intimidation."

Earlier, she had urged protesters to stay on the road until at least midnight.

DUP leader Gavin Robinson said O'Neill was breaking the law by protesting, and had "broken her pledge of office".

Speaking earlier on Sunday, he said "it is shameful that we see on the streets of Portadown, a first minister, a collection of ministers and series of elected representatives who are participating in an unlawful protest".

Sinn Féin has been contacted for comment.

Northern Ireland Secretary Sir Chris Bryant, who returned from the Labour Party conference for talks, urged both sides to "double down on compromise".

He said "nobody should be attending an unlawful protest", but he added it was not his job "to decide whether somebody has or hasn't broken the law".

Sir Chris met politicians from the DUP, the Alliance Party, the Ulster Unionist Party (UUP) and the Social Democratic and Labour Party (SDLP) on Sunday evening.

Sinn Féin said, while they had agreed to meet, the form did not suit the secretary of state. Sir Chris said he had been in discussions with the party's vice president, O'Neill, on Sunday evening.

Sir Chris said "there are a few ideas around" about how to move forward, but that "we haven't got a solution yet".

Earlier on Sunday, Prime Minister Andy Burnham appealed for "calm on all sides", saying there have been "big gains made in Northern Ireland, and we don't want to see things go backwards".

Taoiseach (Irish prime minister) Micheál Martin also appealed for calm, but he said he found the original decision by the Parades Commission to approve the march "incomprehensible and wrong".

While at the protest, First Minister O'Neill was asked if she thought Stormont could collapse over Drumcree.

She replied: "The progress of the last 28 years have been brought into question by the actions of the Orange Order and those within political unionism that want to drag us backwards.

"What's the point? What's the point whenever people are going to railroad over their rights?"

DUP MP Carla Lockhart said the first minister was "whipping up hysteria" at an unlawful protest, and warned of "profound" consequences if the Parade Commission's determination is not upheld.

SDLP leader Claire Hanna, who was at the protest, called for "political leadership" and said it was "necessary to de-escalate". Her party has called for an international mediator to help resolve the dispute.

Meanwhile, UUP leader Jon Burrows said the rule of law needed to apply to "everyone", and that Stormont has been "put under threat".

"It is vital that everyone obeys the law. I don't care who that is. I don't care how senior you are," he said.

Justice Minister Naomi Long, from the Alliance Party, said there was a "predictability about all of this", calling it an "entirely avoidable conflict".

PSNI Chief Constable Jon Boutcher said the policing operation "helped ensure there has been no violence or disorder".

The last 24 hours have been "very challenging for our people", he later told reporters at the Waterfront, adding that the police have been "evidence gathering".

"So whatever's been happening, by whatever party, we've been gathering the evidence of what they've been doing," he said. "So we'll deal with that at the right time."

Boutcher said he wants everybody to find "a place that they can, with dignity, walk away from the current situation", but added that there needs to be a "longer-term conversation".

The Orange Order, the most prominent of the loyal orders associated with Protestants in Northern Ireland, holds thousands of parades every year and the vast majority pass off without incident.

However, many Catholics see the marches as sectarian and object to them passing through, or close to, Catholic or nationalist areas.

The Garvaghy Road had been part of the Drumcree route, but by the mid 1990s nationalist residents protested against the parade.

When the Orange Order was prevented by police from walking down the route in July 1995, there was a tense stand-off. It was the same for the next three years.

Violence related to the dispute resulted in riots, roadblocks and murders across Northern Ireland.

In 1998, the newly-established Parades Commission ruled that the Orange Order should not march down the road - a decision upheld until Friday, when it said the march could go ahead along Garvaghy Road for the first time in 30 years.

Rather than start at 13:00 on Sunday as intended, the commission said it could begin no later than 08:00 - and with 35 participants rather than the 60 the Orange Order requested.

An initial legal challenge from the road's Residents' Coalition (GRRC) at the High Court saw a judge issue an injunction banning the parade - but this was later successfully challenged by an Orange Order member at the Court of Appeal.

Late on Saturday evening, the GRRC was given permission to challenge that decision at the High Court, an appeal which was dismissed by Justice Michael Humphreys.

In a hearing concluding at 02:15 BST on Sunday morning, Justice Humphreys said: "This court cannot substitute its own view or anyone else's view for that of the commission."

articles.title: Kolkata woman 'assaulted, abused' at at five-star hotel nightclub, JW Marriott says venue is third-party run
articles.summary: Pragati Maidan Police arrested 24-year-old Mohammed Rafey Azim for allegedly assaulting and molesting a woman at Toy Room disco inside JW Marriott Kolkata; probe ongoing.
articles.body: KOLKATA: Pragati Maidan cops have arrested a 24-year-old man for allegedly wrongfully restraining, physically assaulting, and outraging the modesty of a young woman at a nightclub inside a prominent five star hotel located along the EM Bypass near Science City in the early hours of Sunday.The arrested suspect has been identified as Mohammed Rafey Azim (24), a resident of Bhukailash Road in Kidderpore and Tiljala Road in the Beniapukur area.According to police, the incident occurred around 2 am on Sunday, when the 20-year-old complainant, a resident of New Alipore , visited the disco located inside the five star property along with a group of eight friends.The victim stated in her complaint that while they were at the venue, the accused, aided and abetted by others, confronted her group. The suspect allegedly subjected the complainant to wrongful restraint, physically assaulted her, and used extremely filthy and abusive language intended to insult her modesty. Following the altercation and physical assault, the accused and his aides fled the scene.The police were alerted through an emergency call at the Dial 100 control room. A team from Pragati Maidan PS immediately rushed to the place of occurrence. Cops said the five star hotel administration helped them in collecting evidence when requested.According to additional CP (crime) Kunal Agarwal, cops arrested the accused as soon as they received the complaint. “After receiving the information from Toy Room Disco located inside JW Marriott Hotel through Dial 100, a team of Pragati Maidan PS visited the place and after examination requested the complainant to submit a complaint. Meanwhile, the complainant and her friends came to Pragati Maidan PS and submitted the plaint letter. On the basis of it, an FIR was started. After lodging the FIR and identifying the address of accused, a raid was conducted and the accused was arrested,” said Agarwal.Pragati Maidan Police registered charges under sections 74 (assault or use of criminal force to woman with intent to outrage her modesty), 79 (word, gesture, or act intended to insult modesty), 115(2) (voluntarily causing hurt), 126(2) (wrongful restraint), and 54 (abettor present when offence is committed) of the BNS.Azim was arrested from his Tiljala Road residence around 11:40 am on Sunday.Gorav Arora, general manager, JW Marriott Kolkata, said: “Toy Room is a third-party managed outsourced venue and the hotel does not operate it. articles.title: DHS announces nationwide surge in ‘sanctuary’ cities
articles.summary: DHS said ICE has initiated a “surge in sanctuary cities,” as part of the Trump administration’s continuous crackdown on immigration.
articles.body:
( NewsNation ) — U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement is ramping up its presence in " sanctuary cities ," which are known to limit cooperation between local law enforcement and federal officers, according to the Department of Homeland Security.

In a statement posted Saturday on X, DHS said ICE has initiated a "surge in sanctuary cities," as part of the Trump administration's continuous crackdown on immigration .

The states and jurisdictions identified by DHS include California, Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware, Washington, D.C., Illinois, Minnesota, New York, Oregon, Rhode Island, Vermont and Washington.

The statement comes a couple of days after federal officials shot a Venezuelan man in his car while he was delivering food for DoorDash in Austin, Texas.

Wilber Rafael Garcas Perez was admitted to a hospital but has been under ICE's custody with a bullet still lodged in his back.

Federal immigration agents have shot at least 20 people since Republican President Donald Trump returned to office, seven of them fatally.

The shootings have sparked protests across the country.

Critics contend that Trump's push to ramp up deportations has led to an increasing number of violent confrontations, and accuse the administration of resisting accountability for the agents involved.

With the surge in ICE presence across the U.S., DHS officials said that they "will continue to arrest any and all illegal aliens that come into our path," and claimed that they are targeting "criminal illegal aliens" who have been "released from jails by sanctuary politicians."

Trump has committed to deporting "the worst of the worst," but the vast majority of people arrested were non-criminal or had minor offenses.

Last week, a U.S. citizen was left bloodied and injured on the side of the road in a Chicago suburb after a confrontation with immigration enforcement agents who mistook him for a fugitive, according to local police and a resident who tried to help the man.

DHS called its recent plan to increase ICE presence in cities a "nationwide public safety surge."

The Associated Press and Reuters contributed to this story.

articles.title: John Healey to promise 'new age of industrialisation' for UK in conference speech
articles.summary: The chancellor will unveil policies aimed at boosting British shipbuilding in his speech to Labour's annual conference on Monday.
articles.body:
John Healey will promise "a new age of industrialisation" for the UK, when he delivers his first Labour conference speech as chancellor on Monday.

Healey will tell delegates "our coal mines are not coming back", but that Labour will remake Britain's industrial past "for the modern age" by backing advanced manufacturing.

He will also announce plans to boost Britain's shipbuilding industry, with new orders for Royal Navy floating docks and a maritime research vessel.

With just a month to go until his first Budget, the chancellor is under pressure to cut spending or raise taxes to tackle the ballooning cost of government borrowing.

But he is not expected to reveal any details about his Budget plans in his speech at Labour's annual conference in Liverpool.

Instead, he will attempt to set out a positive vision for the future of British industry, based around what he will call a "new confidence in Britain".

The former defence secretary will announce that three new floating docks at HM Royal Naval Base Clyde, at Faslane, will be built in the UK, rather than put out to international tender.

Plans for the new docks were first set out in 2023 and are expected to upgrade Faslane's facilities for the next generation of British submarines.

The docks form part of a wider £15bn upgrade programme for the Royal Navy's shipyards and are expected to come into service in the early 2030s.

First Secretary of State Louise Haigh said in a speech on Sunday that the government would also commission a new marine research vessel as part of plans for a "new era of reindustrialisation".

The chancellor is expected to announce £115m in funding for the ship, which is also set to come into service in the early 2030s.

Ahead of his speech, Healey said: "By backing British shipyards, we are not only boosting national security but also securing resilience in the industries that will drive growth today while building the capabilities the country needs for the future."

Shadow chancellor Andrew Griffith said the plans were "reheated announcements" with "no clarity on where the money is coming from".

He added: "Labour are running scared of making the tough choices needed to pay for Britain's defence.

"All they can offer is reannounced docks and more hot air from Healey. Only the Conservatives will cut the welfare bill to fund defence."

Charlotte Brumpton-Childs, national secretary of the GMB union, which has campaigned for the move, said it would be a "massive boost" for the UK's shipbuilding sector.

"For too long juicy contracts have been sent to overseas - often subsidised - yards.

"This policy could reinvigorate UK yards and the communities that depend on them," he added.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham - who is due to deliver his big conference speech on Tuesday - has previously spoken about his ambition to "reindustrialise" Britain, including in talks last week with US President Donald Trump.

But in a survey to be published on Monday, the Confederation of British Industry (CBI) will highlight falling economic activity across key sectors such as retail and services in the three months to September, with manufacturing declining more moderately.

CBI deputy chief economist Alpesh Paleja said rising energy and employment costs combined with weak demand were continuing to put pressure on profit margins.

He added: "Uncertainty ahead of next month's Budget is also holding back activity in some sectors.

"Against the backdrop of renewed fiscal pressures, the Budget must draw a clear red line under any more rises in the cost of hiring, investing and doing business."

The chancellor is also under pressure from some of Labour's trade union backers to do more to tackle the cost of living.

Sharon Graham, general secretary of the Unite union, has called on Healey to "do something for workers and the working class" in his Budget.

She urged him to unfreeze income tax thresholds "to put money back into people's pockets" and take further action on energy bills.

In his conference speech, Healey will also announce plans to bring back a training scheme run by trade unions, to help workers in England gain new skills and adapt as technology, including AI, changes the workplace.

The Union Learning Fund will get £15m in taxpayers' money, taken from existing government budgets.

Employees do not need to be union members to benefit, with support options ranging from essential English, maths and digital skills, to training for jobs in growing industries, such as advanced manufacturing.

articles.title: Pope pledges action on clergy child abuse in meeting with French survivors
articles.summary: Head of the Roman Catholic Church holds ’emotional’ two-hour meeting with seven survivors in French town of Lourdes.
articles.body:
Pope Leo XIV has thanked a group of survivors of clerical abuse “for their painful testimony” and “reaffirmed his commitment” to end harm by Catholic priests at a meeting in southwestern France, the Vatican said.

The leader of the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics is on a four-day visit to France .

On Sunday, the pontiff visited the pilgrimage town of Lourdes, where he privately met seven survivors of child abuse, now adults, and promised to further efforts to reform the Church in the wake of the global sexual abuse scandal .

The group said in a later news conference that the meeting was emotional and touching.

“When he saw the state I was in, he took me into his arms,” survivor Jean-Marie Delbos said, adding, “It was an extraordinary moment.”

The 80-year-old was abused as a pupil at the nearby boarding school of Notre-Dame de Betharram, where staff have been accused of physical and sexual abuse over several decades.

The survivors said they felt heard and that they were impressed by Leo’s compassion and knowledge of their individual cases.

But they hoped the words would be accompanied by action.

Jerome Guillement, who has written about a priest abusing him as a teenager, said at the news conference that the pope understood the “systemic” nature of sexual abuse in the Church.

“From his point of view, the perpetrators are individuals, but what allows it to continue is the systemic dimension within the institution,” he said.

“He certainly believes that the Church has done a great deal in France, but he also believes that the Church in France still has a tremendous amount left to do.”

Local leaders hoped Leo’s visit would help repair the Church’s standing after a 2021 independent inquiry found that some 330,000 French children had been abused by Catholic clergy and lay leaders over seven decades.

The pope told an estimated 150,000 people gathered for a Mass in a field near the famed Catholic shrine in Lourdes earlier on Sunday that the Church must have the courage to face its past.

Veronique Garnier, another survivor who met with the pontiff, said she had found the Mass, in which Leo referred to abuse without directly apologising for it, troubling and wondered why she had attended.

But she said she was encouraged by her meeting with Leo.

“I do indeed believe there is hope – hope that there can be change and truly listening to us at a deep level, rather than just superficially, with beautiful words that are never followed by any real action,” she said.

Leo also spoke about the abuse scandals in a closed-door meeting with French bishops on Sunday, according to a Vatican-provided text.

Leo calls assisted dying ‘false compassion’

The pontiff also condemned France’s legalisation of medically assisted death in July as immoral “false compassion” during his visit to the Lourdes shrine associated with miraculous healings on Sunday, his third day in France.

The pope sought to encourage people who live in “terrible pain” that they have inherent dignity that no law or algorithm can eliminate.

“What is legal is not necessarily moral,” Leo said at the Mass, drawing applause from the crowd.

Catholic teaching holds that all human life must be protected from conception until natural death, leading to its firm opposition to abortion, euthanasia and medically assisted dying.

articles.title: You need £17,000 for a first home - here's how to save it
articles.summary: Here are four ways you can put money aside to save enough for a deposit on your first home.
articles.body:
If buying your own home is the finishing line, then saving up the money to get there is a marathon.

The "Your First Home" scheme , announced on Saturday, aims to help first-time buyers in England get on the housing ladder with a small deposit.

Currently a 5% deposit on the current average UK house price of £272,000 plus moving costs and legal fees - will set you back about £16,850, according to financial information service Moneyfacts.

That's daunting, but here are four ways that experts say you can at least make a start on saving for a deposit.

Depositing an amount you can afford into a regular savers account the day after you are paid is a good way to start, suggests Anna Bowes, savings expert at financial advisers The Private Office.

"It becomes like another bill, but one that you can benefit from in the future," she says.

The type of account that's suitable depends on your circumstances.

Some of the ones which pay the highest interest are only accessible if you hold a current account with the provider, she says.

Other considerations are whether you can lock the money away for longer, to receive a better savings rate.

If you don't have a buffer of other savings, then experts say an easy access account gives you the chance to dip into the money to pay an unexpected bill.

You can save up to £4,000 a year in a Lifetime Individual Savings Account (LISA) and the government guarantees a 25% bonus. So, if you put the full amount in then the government will add £1,000 a year.

But there is a catch, that has left some people out of pocket .

Money saved in a LISA can only be used to buy a first home up to the value of £450,000 - a threshold that has not changed since 2017.

The only other time you can withdraw the money is after the age of 60 or in the exceptional case that you are terminally ill with less than 12 months to live.

Withdrawal under any other circumstances means you get hit with a penalty - so you could get back less than you put in.

Ministers are planning to replace the LISA with a new First Time Buyer ISA, but there are no clear details yet about how it will work.

'I lost thousands in savings and my partner's money is in limbo'

The earlier you start saving the more you can build up thanks to the magic of compound interest. In short, interest is added on a larger and larger pot as time goes by.

Bowes says that saving £50 a month from the age of 20 would give you about £41,000 in 30 years' time when you hit 50, assuming interest of 5% is paid a year.

Start 10 years later, and you'd need to save more than double - £101 a month - to have the same amount at the age of 50.

Investing in stocks and shares is another option , but the value of investments can go down as well as up.

An increasing number of lenders are offering mortgage deals with little or no deposit required.

David Hollingworth, from L&C, points to mortgages that have deposits starting from £5,000 and allow people to borrow up to 98% or 99% of the property purchase price.

They might not always be the best option , and not everyone will be eligible.

And, of course, some first-time buyers turn to their parents for help.

Again that's not available to all , but a survey by the Nationwide Building Society suggests that more than half of parents who charge their adult children rent are putting some or all of the money towards helping their child save to buy their own home.

articles.title: An expert guide to finding the perfect pillow for your sleeping position
articles.summary: Dr Chris McCarthy talks through the four considerations you need to make before buying your pillow.
articles.body:
"I am one of those people," says Dr Chris McCarthy. "I do take my pillow with me."

You may have seen those people at the airport - a pillow stuffed under an arm as they drag their suitcases to check-in.

Or you might be one yourself - attached to a pillow that's soft enough to settle into but robust enough that it's not bunched into a ball by morning.

McCarthy insists he's not being fussy. He's a top physiotherapist and knows the wrong pillow can be a pain in the neck.

He doesn't take his abroad, but as soon as he gets to his hotel he starts "faffing about" with the pillows - and he's got a tried and tested trick to make even the most lacklustre one fit for sleep. Here's his guide to choosing the perfect pillow for you.

McCarthy, an associate professor at the Manchester School of Physiotherapy, says the right pillow will depend on what position you sleep in.

He tells the BBC's Sliced Bread podcast that most people fall into one of three categories of sleeper: side, back or front.

McCarthy discourages front sleeping as your neck is turned one way for a long period of time.

"Inevitably a muscle or ligament gets stretched and a bit irritated," he says. "If there's one thing there's a really good consensus on... in the physiotherapy world about treating spinal pain, it's don't sleep on your front."

When choosing a pillow, back sleepers should consider the flexion at the top of their spine, a curving that increases naturally in many people as they age.

If you have a bigger bend "it means you need a slightly thicker pillow than someone who's got a very flat back," says McCarthy.

For side sleepers the key measurement is the width of your shoulders. In general, the broader you are the thicker the pillow you will need. But you also need to consider your mattress.

McCarthy says how much you sink into your mattress "makes a huge difference in the subsequent height you then need from the pillow".

"Broad shoulders need a thick pillow [if] you're on a very firm mattress," he explains.

"If you're on a softer mattress, then you need a thinner pillow because your shoulder sinks into the mattress [more]."

This is less of an issue for back sleepers as they don't sink into the mattress as much as side sleepers do.

If your pillow feels too flat, McCarthy suggests placing a folded towel underneath and changing the number of folds to adjust the height. Then you can make a rough measurement to help you pick a new one.

Specialist pillows are often advertised as contoured, ergonomic or orthopaedic - but McCarthy says their effectiveness isn't completely proven.

"There is a little bit of fairly scrappy evidence to suggest that having a little bit of a higher front of the pillow, which goes into the neck area... does help [side sleepers]."

To see if a higher front helps you sleep better, you can try McCarthy's towel trick by rolling it and placing it underneath your pillow.

He urges side sleepers to pick a position that keeps their back straight.

For back sleepers, some manufacturers advertise a pillow with a dip in the middle that is raised at the sides. It does put people into a good sleeping position, says McCarthy, but some of his patients have found them "a bit claustrophobic".

Someone who has a large and heavy head also needs a thicker and firmer pillow, he adds.

Feather and down can keep you cool on warm nights because they wick away heat from your head, says McCarthy.

But they can change shape during the night, particularly if the sleeper moves around a lot and the pillow can end up bunched towards the headboard.

"What starts off as a nice, flat, supported surface becomes a wedge and so your neck is then kinked up."

Hollow fibre and microfibre fillings can hold shape better though they generally don't wick away heat as well, says McCarthy.

Some are made with a firmer material in the lower half of the pillow, which help retain the shape during the night.

McCarthy bought his foam pillow, which has tubular spaces for ventilation, five years ago for about £50. As a side sleeper, he adjusts its height using a folded towel laid underneath it.

He says choosing the right pillow is very much "horses for courses" and encourages people to utilise the trial period some manufacturers offer customers.

"There just isn't a one-off design that is perfect for everybody or every position, I'm afraid," he says. "You really have to personalise it."

articles.title: Previsão do tempo RS: chuva volumosa e alerta de ciclone | G1
articles.standfirst: Defesa Civil do Estado apontou áreas com risco severo para chuva intensa, além riscos de tempestades com queda de granizo e rajadas de vento.
articles.summary: Com risco de granizo e ventos de 90 km/h, a previsão do tempo no RS alerta para chuva volumosa e formação de ciclone entre esta segunda e terça-feira.
articles.body:
A semana começa com previsão de instabilidade em diferentes regiões do Rio Grande do Sul, segundo a Climatempo. A Defesa Civil do Estado apontou áreas com risco severo para chuva intensa e volumosa, além de riscos de tempestades com queda de granizo e rajadas de vento.

Para segunda-feira (28), a tendência é de agravamento das condições meteorológicas com aprofundamento da área de baixa pressão e o início da organização de um sistema atmosférico entre o continente e a Região Sul.

A previsão aponta risco de novos temporais com granizo e rajadas superiores a 90 km/h . Os acumulados de chuva podem variar entre 20 e 100 milímetros, com possibilidade de ultrapassar 130 milímetros em localidades da Campanha e do Oeste.

Na Região Metropolitana de Porto Alegre, a segunda-feira será de muita nebulosidade e chuva, com possibilidade de pancadas fortes e temporais . A região também fica inserida na área de instabilidade mais abrangente sobre o Estado.

Conforme a Defesa Civil, algumas áreas dessas regiões podem registrar mais de 120 milímetros de chuva em apenas 12 horas e volumes acima de 170 milímetros em 24 horas.

São Gabriel aparece entre os municípios com maior acumulado previsto para segunda-feira, com cerca de 82 milímetros. Também há previsão de chuva expressiva em São Sepé (69 mm), Rosário do Sul (63 mm), Santana do Livramento (60 mm) e Santa Maria (60 mm).

Nos Vales, os volumes podem chegar a 55 milímetros em Vera Cruz, 53 milímetros em Cachoeira do Sul e 51 milímetros em Santa Cruz do Sul.

Na terça-feira (29), a formação e o desenvolvimento de um ciclone associado a uma frente fria devem manter a atmosfera instável sobre o estado.

A Campanha e a Fronteira Oeste concentram os maiores acumulados previstos. Dom Pedrito pode registrar cerca de 115 milímetros de chuva, seguido por Santana do Livramento (105 mm) e Bagé (87 mm).

Também são esperados volumes elevados em Candiota (73 mm), Pinheiro Machado (71 mm), Quaraí (71 mm) e Barra do Quaraí (67 mm). Na região Sul, Pelotas e Capão do Leão podem receber cerca de 60 milímetros de chuva.

A Defesa Civil alerta que na terça-feira continuam as condições para temporais severos e chuva forte em áreas do Oeste, Centro e metade Norte do estado.

Balanço divulgado no final da tarde deste domingo pela Defesa Civil apresenta aumento nos estragos espalhados pelo RS em razão da forte chuva de granizo: 9,5 mil pessoas afetadas, 2,2 mil casas danificadas e um ferido.

Em Santiago , foram 5 mil pessoas afetadas. Em Alegrete, 2 mil moradores, incluindo 1 ferido e deixando 10 pessoas desabrigadas. Em Capão do Cipó, 820 pessoas foram afetadas, e Catuípe, 800 moradores.

Vídeos mostram a intensidade da precipitação em Santiago no sábado. Veja acima.

Em alguns pontos da cidade, o volume de granizo foi tão grande que o chão ficou praticamente branco , como se estivesse coberto por uma camada de gelo.

Forte chuva de granizo em Santiago, no RS — Foto: Imagens cedidas/ Bibiana Thones

Balanço da Defesa Civil divulgado na tarde deste domingo (27):

9.517 pessoas afetadas (5 mil pessoas em Santiago; 2 mil pessoas em Alegrete)

Nenhum óbito confirmado, em investigação ou desaparecido

2.2 mil casas danificadas (1 mil casas em Santiago; 700 em Alegrete)

A instabilidade começou a avançar sobre a Fronteira Oeste do Rio Grande do Sul na tarde deste sábado.

Em Barra do Quaraí, houve registro de chuva com granizo . Já em Uruguaiana , um temporal chegou à região no início da noite.

Os fenômenos ocorrem em meio aos alertas emitidos pelo Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet), pela Climatempo e pela Defesa Civil Estadual, que já apontavam risco de instabilidade entre esta sexta-feira (25) e a próxima segunda-feira (28) .

De acordo com os avisos meteorológicos, a mudança no tempo está associada à atuação de uma área de baixa pressão localizada entre o norte da Argentina e o Paraguai . Esse sistema favorece o transporte de ar quente e úmido em direção ao Rio Grande do Sul, criando condições para a formação de temporais.

Chegada de tempestade em Uruguaiana nesse sábado (26) — Foto: Pablo Gimenes/ RBS TV

articles.body:
Os candidatos ao governo do Rio de Janeiro nas Eleições 2026 cumprem compromissos de campanha nesta segunda-feira (28).

Desde o dia 16 de agosto, os candidatos estão liberados para atos de campanha, como a realização de comícios, carreatas, passeatas, distribuição de material gráfico e propaganda pela internet.

Confira a agenda de cada um dos 9 candidatos para esta quinta-feira, em ordem alfabética:

14h: Panfletagem no Calçadão de Nilópolis, na esquina da Rua Professor Alfredo Filgueiras com a Avenida Mirandela.

17h: Panfletagem em Marechal Hermes, próximo à Batata de Marechal.

O candidato não tem agenda pública prevista para esta segunda-feira.

12h: Panfletagem em frente ao Edifício Senado (Edisen), da Petrobras, no Centro do Rio.

10h: Corpo a corpo com eleitores da Praça Saens Peña até o Shopping Tijuca, na Zona Norte do Rio. A concentração será na esquina das ruas General Roca e Conde de Bonfim, em frente ao Banco do Brasil.

13h30: Caminhada na Praça Seca, na Zona Oeste do Rio, e anúncio de propostas para a área de segurança pública. A concentração será na Rua Cândido Benício, 2.762, próximo à estação Ipase do BRT.

6h: Panfletagem nas proximidades de uma fábrica de moda íntima, na Penha, Zona Norte do Rio.

11h30: Panfletagem nas proximidades da Unisuam, na Avenida Paris, 84, em Bonsucesso.

17h: Participação em ato na Cinelândia, no Centro do Rio.

A equipe de campanha não divulgou a agenda do candidato para esta segunda-feira.

articles.title: Quando é o quinto dia útil de outubro de 2026? Veja data | G1
articles.standfirst: Confira quando cai o quinto dia útil de outubro de 2026 e a data limite para o pagamento do salário.
articles.summary: Confira quando cai o quinto dia útil de outubro de 2026 e a data limite para o pagamento do salário.
articles.body:
Confira quando cai o quinto dia útil de outubro de 2026 e a data limite para o pagamento do salário. — Foto: Rafa Neddermeyer/Agência Brasil

Para trabalhadores com carteira assinada, o quinto dia útil de outubro de 2026 será terça-feira, dia 6 . Para o cálculo do prazo de pagamento de salários, o sábado é considerado dia útil, enquanto domingos e feriados não entram na contagem.

A regra está prevista no artigo 459 da Consolidação das Leis do Trabalho (CLT), que determina que o salário deve ser pago, no máximo, até o quinto dia útil do mês seguinte ao trabalhado.

Quando é o quinto dia útil de outubro de 2026?

No cálculo do prazo para pagamento do salário, são considerados os dias de segunda-feira a sábado. Domingos e feriados ficam fora da contagem.

Primeiro dia útil: 1º de outubro (quinta-feira);

Segundo dia útil: 2 de outubro (sexta-feira);

Terceiro dia útil: 3 de outubro (sábado);

Quarto dia útil: 5 de outubro (segunda-feira);

Quinto dia útil: 6 de outubro (terça-feira).

Portanto, para quem trabalha com carteira assinada, o quinto dia útil de outubro de 2026 é 6 de outubro.

Sábado conta como dia útil para o pagamento do salário?

Sim. Para a contagem do prazo previsto na CLT para o pagamento de salários, o sábado é considerado dia útil.

A contagem é interrompida aos domingos e feriados. Por isso, mesmo que o trabalhador não tenha expediente aos sábados, o dia entra no cálculo do quinto dia útil.

Essa regra é específica para o prazo de pagamento do salário e não significa que o sábado seja necessariamente um dia normal de trabalho para todos os empregados.

O que acontece se o salário não for pago até o quinto dia útil?

O artigo 459 da CLT estabelece o prazo máximo para o pagamento do salário. Se o empregador não cumprir a data-limite, o trabalhador pode buscar orientação para cobrar os valores atrasados.

Em caso de atraso, o empregado pode recorrer à Justiça do Trabalho para cobrar o pagamento devido, com os acréscimos que forem aplicáveis. O sindicato da categoria também pode auxiliar na defesa dos direitos dos trabalhadores e na adoção das medidas cabíveis.

Atrasos frequentes ou prolongados no pagamento podem caracterizar descumprimento das obrigações do empregador.

Dependendo das circunstâncias e da gravidade da situação, isso pode levar ao reconhecimento da rescisão indireta, quando o trabalhador encerra o contrato por falta grave do empregador e pode ter direito às verbas de uma demissão sem justa causa.

O empregador também pode estar sujeito à fiscalização e às penalidades previstas na legislação trabalhista.

articles.title: Unimed Costa do Sol amplia atendimento em transtornos do neurodesenvolvimento | G1
articles.standfirst: Nova unidade do Viver Bem, em Macaé, ampliou a capacidade de atendimento em até 670 pa-cientes e fortaleceu o acompanhamento multiprofissional, fortalecendo o cuidado especializado.
articles.summary: Nova unidade do Viver Bem, em Macaé, ampliou a capacidade de atendimento em até 670 pa-cientes e fortaleceu o acompanhamento multiprofissional, fortalecendo o cuidado especializado.
articles.body:
Ambientes amplos favorecem o atendimento integrado e a troca entre profissionais — Foto: Fotógrafo Júlio Teixeira

A Unimed Costa do Sol ampliou a assistência a pacientes com transtornos do neurodesenvolvimento com a inauguração, no dia 3 de setembro de 2026, da nova unidade do Viver Bem, no Centro de Macaé, norte fluminense. Com uma estrutura de 15 salas de atendimento e capacidade para receber aproximadamente 670 novos pacientes, o espaço foi criado para acompanhar o crescimento da demanda e oferecer um ambiente mais acolhedor, confortável e preparado para as diferentes necessidades dos beneficiários e suas famílias.

A nova unidade passou a integrar a estrutura de atendimento terapêutico especializado da cooperativa, oferecendo acompanhamento multiprofissional para pessoas com Transtorno do Espectro do Autismo (TEA), outros transtornos do neurodesenvolvimento e transtornos comportamentais. O serviço também atende pessoas com sinais de alerta para o TEA, com acompanhamento individualizado de acordo com as necessidades e particularidades de cada beneficiário, independentemente da faixa etária.

Um espaço pensado para ampliar o cuidado

Segundo a gerente de Recursos Próprios da Unimed Costa do Sol, Rayssa Martins, a expansão foi motivada pelo crescimento do serviço e pelo aumento da demanda.

“A nova Unidade do Viver Bem representou um passo importante no atendimento aos nossos beneficiários. A criação desse espaço surgiu a partir do crescimento desse serviço e do aumento da demanda, trazendo a oportunidade de ampliarmos a nossa capacidade de atendimento e de oferecermos uma estrutura ainda mais acolhedora e confortável aos pacientes e suas famílias”, explicou.

nauguração da unidade reuniu autoridades locais e representantes da Unimed — Foto: Fotógrafo Júlio Teixeira

A estrutura conta com 15 salas de atendimento e capacidade aproximada para atender pelo menos 670 pacientes. Considerando a média de atendimentos, a unidade tem potencial para realizar cerca de 6.700 atendimentos por mês, ampliando a oferta de terapias e o acesso ao cuidado especializado. O atendimento será realizado de forma integrada por profissionais de oito especialidades: fisioterapia, fonoaudiologia, nutrição, psicologia, psicomotricidade, psicopedagogia, musicoterapia e terapia ocupacional.

Um dos diferenciais da estrutura é a sala destinada à terapia ocupacional e fisioterapia. Por serem ambientes amplos, os espaços permitem a realização de atendimentos de forma transdisciplinar, favorecendo o trabalho conjunto dos profissionais, a troca de conhecimentos e a construção compartilhada de estratégias para cada paciente.

Essa configuração possibilita um olhar ainda mais integrado sobre as necessidades individuais, fortalecendo a atuação multiprofissional e a busca por melhores resultados no desenvolvimento, na autonomia e na qualidade de vida dos pacientes.

A nova estrutura também amplia a assistência aos recém-nascidos e bebês prematuros. A pediatra Dra. Darlene Rodrigues Daumas, responsável pelo acompanhamento desse público, destacou a importância da continuidade do cuidado após a alta hospitalar.

“Os bebês prematuros são muito especiais. São indivíduos que passaram por momentos muito difíceis dentro de uma UTI, onde foi investido muito e que, ao terem alta, deixam as famílias perdidas: ‘E agora, o que será do meu bebê?’. Por isso, é importante esse acompanhamento pós-alta, que era uma iniciativa que já vínhamos pleiteando e que a diretoria nos deu a oportunidade de realizar”, afirmou.

A unidade realiza o acompanhamento desde o momento da alta hospitalar até o segundo ano de vida. Para a pediatra, o principal objetivo é contribuir para que cada criança possa alcançar seu máximo potencial.

“O principal objetivo é alcançar o máximo potencial que essas crianças têm. Tenho certeza de que essa unidade não vai olhar para a criança apenas pelo problema que ela traz, mas por todo o potencial que ela ainda pode alcançar”, ressaltou.

Antes da inauguração do novo espaço, as três unidades do Viver Bem da cooperativa já acompanhavam 920 pacientes. Com a abertura da nova unidade em Macaé, a Unimed Costa do Sol ampliou a capacidade de atendimento e fortaleceu sua assistência própria, possibilitando que mais beneficiários tivessem acesso a terapias e acompanhamento multiprofissional.

De acordo com o diretor-presidente da Unimed Costa do Sol, Dr. Gumercino Pinheiro Faria Filho, o projeto vinha sendo planejado havia algum tempo e refletia a preocupação da cooperativa com o crescimento das demandas relacionadas ao neurodesenvolvimento.

“Esse espaço foi pensado já tem um tempo. Precisamos agradecer ao Conselho de Administração da Cooperativa pela aprovação desse projeto, entendendo que a Unimed tem um diferencial em relação aos outros planos de saúde. A preocupação crescente com as alterações do neurodesenvolvimento, cada dia maiores, nos fez entender e projetar um crescimento das unidades”, destacou.

O diretor-presidente também ressaltou que a cooperativa já trabalhava na preparação de uma nova unidade em Rio das Ostras.

“Estamos preparando mais uma em Rio das Ostras, e essa daqui foi feita com muito carinho, na nossa cidade-sede. A Unimed não é uma operadora de plano de saúde comum. É uma operadora que visa o paciente, que busca atender bem as pessoas, com um atendimento humanizado, e que precisa ter preocupação com o desenvolvimento dessas crianças e com a qualidade de vida”, afirmou.

Cuidado integrado reúne diferentes profissionais para atender às necessidades de cada paciente — Foto: Fotógrafo Júlio Teixeira

A proposta do Viver Bem foi oferecer um ambiente estruturado e acolhedor, no qual profissionais de diferentes áreas atuassem de maneira integrada para compreender as necessidades de cada paciente e definir estratégias de cuidado individualizadas.

O acompanhamento considerou as particularidades e o ritmo de cada pessoa, buscando favorecer o desenvolvimento de habilidades, a autonomia e a qualidade de vida.

Para Rayssa Martins, a inauguração representou a continuidade de um trabalho desenvolvido pela cooperativa com foco em um modelo de cuidado cada vez mais integrado.

“Mais do que um novo espaço físico, essa inauguração representou a evolução de um trabalho que já vinha sendo construído e o compromisso da Unimed em continuar investindo em um cuidado cada vez mais integral, humanizado e próximo”, afirmou.

A inauguração também contou com a presença do prefeito de Macaé, Welberth Rezende, que destacou a importância da ampliação de serviços de saúde para o desenvolvimento da cidade.

“Fiquei feliz de poder participar diretamente, porque, na verdade, a gente se complementa. Os serviços que são oferecidos aqui qualificam ainda mais a nossa cidade. Macaé é uma cidade referência hoje, em pleno desenvolvimento”, declarou.

O prefeito também citou indicadores relacionados ao desenvolvimento econômico do município. Segundo ele, Macaé foi a 1ª cidade em geração de emprego em 2025, de acordo com o Cadastro Geral de Empregados e Desempregados (CAGED), e concentrou 1/3 de todo o investimento privado.

Nesse cenário, destacou a importância da criação de uma rede de serviços que oferecesse suporte à população e contribuísse para que os moradores encontrassem na cidade um espaço de acolhimento e assistência.

“Na área da saúde, a Unimed Costa do Sol é um dos maiores parceiros da Prefeitura, porque acaba trazendo soluções em uma área de fundamental importância. A Unimed, além de ser um grande parceiro, qualifica a cidade com serviços e é parceira no dia a dia”, afirmou.

Welberth Rezende também destacou a atenção da cooperativa às necessidades da população. “A Unimed, antenada ao momento que a sociedade vive, montou um espaço específico para atender com todo carinho, afeto e acolhimento”, ressaltou.

O Transtorno do Espectro do Autismo (TEA) é uma condição do neurodesenvolvimento que pode impactar a comunicação, a interação social e o comportamento. No Brasil, o Censo 2022, realizado pelo Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE), investigou a população com Transtorno do Espectro Autista e identificou 2,4 milhões de pessoas com o transtorno.

Os dados reforçaram a importância da ampliação do acesso a serviços especializados e do acompanhamento multiprofissional, especialmente diante da necessidade de oferecer assistência individualizada e contínua.

Localizada na Rua Dr. Júlio Olivier, 476, no Centro de Macaé, a nova unidade funcionou de segunda a sexta-feira, das 8h às 20h. Os beneficiários que possuíam guias para a realização de terapias puderam realizar o agendamento diretamente na unidade. A medida buscou facilitar o acesso aos serviços e proporcionar mais agilidade no direcionamento dos atendimentos.

Com a nova estrutura, a Unimed Costa do Sol ampliou a oferta de atendimento especializado e fortaleceu a assistência às crianças e adolescentes com transtornos do neurodesenvolvimento, aumentando a capacidade de atendimento e o acesso ao acompanhamento multiprofissional.

A Unimed Costa do Sol está presente em toda a região, oferecendo unidades que garantiram acesso facilitado e serviços de qualidade. Em Macaé, a cooperativa conta com 8 postos de coleta, o Hospital Unimed Costa do Sol – Unidade Glória, sede administrativa, Centro de Estudos e Pesquisas, espaços Viver Bem Infantil e Espaço Viver Bem, além do serviço de remoção.

Em Rio das Ostras, a cooperativa dispõe do Posto de Coleta 3, Atendimento Administrativo, Centro de Especialidades Terapêuticas, Centro de Especialidades Médicas e Viver Bem Infantil. Em Barra de São João, funciona o Posto de Coleta 7 e, em Casimiro de Abreu, o Posto de Coleta 8 com Atendimento Administrativo, fortalecendo a parceria com a cidade.

Com hospital próprio, laboratório de análises clínicas, postos de coleta, centros de terapias, centro de especialidades médicas, atendimento domiciliar, serviço de remoção e programas de medicina preventiva, a Unimed Costa do Sol se consolidou como referência em saúde suplementar para mais de 100 mil beneficiários, 503 cooperados e mais de 100 estabelecimentos credenciados, estando presente em Macaé, Rio das Ostras, Casimiro de Abreu, Conceição de Macabu, Quissamã e Carapebus.

articles.title: Em Petrópolis, cooperação gera oportunidades e amplia o cuidado  | G1
articles.standfirst: Nutricionista encontra a receita para uma carreira mais saudável em cooperativa de saúde.
articles.summary: Nutricionista encontra a receita para uma carreira mais saudável em cooperativa de saúde.
articles.body:
O nutricionista Luis Felipe Prates faz cerca de 50 atendimentos por semana em Petrópolis — Foto: Anderson Pires

Cuidar de pessoas também pode ser um grande negócio quando quem trabalha cresce junto. No cooperativismo de saúde, conhecimento, experiência e oportunidades são compartilhados para fortalecer profissionais e ampliar o acesso da população aos serviços. Um modelo que reúne 695 cooperativas, mais de 304 mil cooperados e 162 mil empregos e que movimentou R$ 130,7 bilhões em 2025.

Presente em mais de 90% do território nacional e responsável pelo atendimento de mais de 27 milhões de brasileiros, o cooperativismo de saúde mostra, na prática, que é possível conciliar desenvolvimento profissional, geração de renda e cuidado com as pessoas.

Em Petrópolis, na Região Serrana do Rio, Luis Felipe Chaves Prates encontrou nesse modelo uma oportunidade para mudar sua trajetória. Nutricionista há mais de duas décadas, ele buscava mais flexibilidade e novas possibilidades profissionais quando conheceu a Unifop, Cooperativa de Saúde Mental e Reabilitação. Há 16 anos, fez uma escolha que transformou sua forma de trabalhar.

“Trabalhava como CLT na capital, mas, por questões pessoais, buscava uma rotina profissional mais flexível. Quando retornei a Petrópolis, encontrei na cooperativa novas oportunidades de atuação e, principalmente, um ambiente voltado para servir ao próximo, algo que sempre fez parte do meu perfil. Foi assim que me encantei pelo cooperativismo e, em pouco tempo, ampliei minha atuação, passando de cinco para 50 atendimentos por semana”, disse o nutricionista.

O crescimento de Luis ajuda a traduzir em números o que o cooperativismo pode representar na vida de um profissional. Mais do que encontrar espaço para trabalhar, ele passou a fazer parte de uma rede em que diferentes especialidades se complementam, experiências são compartilhadas e o desenvolvimento de um abre caminho para o crescimento de todos.

Na Unifop, são mais de 120 cooperados atuando em diferentes especialidades. Profissionais que poderiam disputar o mesmo espaço de mercado encontraram outra forma de fazer negócio: cooperar para ampliar oportunidades, fortalecer suas carreiras e oferecer um atendimento cada vez mais completo aos pacientes.

“Entendo que, na nutrição, cada nutriente possui um papel fundamental, e, no cooperativismo, não é diferente. O crescimento individual de cada profissional contribui para o desenvolvimento de todo o grupo, em uma experiência que ensina, transforma e produz valores para toda a vida. Como bom nutricionista, posso dizer que esse é um modelo de negócio bastante ‘saudável’”, brincou Luis Felipe.

É justamente essa capacidade de unir pessoas em torno de interesses comuns que faz do cooperativismo um modelo de negócio diferente. Na saúde, profissionais mantêm sua autonomia, mas ganham a força de uma estrutura coletiva para ampliar sua atuação, compartilhar conhecimento e chegar a mais pessoas. Na outra ponta, pacientes encontram uma rede de profissionais que trabalha de forma integrada para cuidar do que mais importa: a vida.

Para o presidente do Sistema OCB/RJ, Vinicius Mesquita, o cooperativismo mostra que valorizar quem cuida também é uma forma de melhorar o cuidado oferecido à sociedade.

“Saúde é feita por pessoas, e o cooperativismo começa justamente pela valorização delas. Quando profissionais se unem, compartilham conhecimento e constroem oportunidades juntos, todos ganham. Ganha o cooperado, que fortalece sua carreira e seu negócio; ganha a cooperativa, que cresce de forma sustentável; e ganha a população, que encontra profissionais preparados e uma rede comprometida com o cuidado. É um modelo de negócio que coloca as pessoas no centro e transforma essa união em desenvolvimento”, destaca Vinicius.

A história de Luis Felipe e sua relação com a Unifop fazem parte do Momento SomosCoop, série produzida pelo Sistema OCB/RJ para mostrar, por meio de histórias reais, como o cooperativismo transforma trajetórias, fortalece negócios e gera desenvolvimento nas comunidades onde está presente.

Sede na Unifop, cooperativa de saúde mental e de reabilitação — Foto: Anderson Pires

O SomosCoop é o movimento nacional de valorização do cooperativismo. A iniciativa conecta cooperativas, cooperados e a sociedade em torno de um propósito: tornar o Coop cada vez mais conhecido e reconhecido e mostrar os impactos positivos desse modelo de negócio para quem produz, trabalha, empreende e consome.

O movimento também convida o consumidor a fazer parte desse ciclo. Ao escolher produtos e serviços de cooperativas, ele contribui para a geração de trabalho, renda e desenvolvimento local. O carimbo SomosCoop ajuda a identificar produtos e serviços cooperativistas e torna essa escolha mais simples no dia a dia. Detalhes sobre o cooperativismo e seu avanço, são encontrados no site

articles.title: CasaCor Brasília: mostra de design e arquitetura vai até 12 de outubro na Casa do Candango | G1
articles.standfirst: Edição deste ano tem 40 ambientes, projetados por 52 profissionais sob o tema 'Mente e Coração'.
articles.summary: Edição deste ano tem 40 ambientes, projetados por 52 profissionais sob o tema 'Mente e Coração'.
articles.body:
Ambienta CASACOR Brasília 2026 — Foto: Divulgação

Até dia 12 de outubro, a Casa do Candango, localizada na 603 Sul, recebe a 34ª edição da CASACOR Brasília – mostra de arquitetura, design de interiores e paisagismo.

Com o tema "Mente e Coração", a 34ª edição da mostra parte da ideia de que o lar deixou de ser apenas um lugar para morar, e tornou-se refúgio físico e emocional, ambiente de cura, convivência e bem-estar.

Esta proposta atravessa praticamente todos os projetos, que exploram a neuroarquitetura, a biofilia, a valorização das memórias afetivas, a integração entre os ambientes e o uso de materiais naturais.

A mostra ocupa o espaço de três pavimentos, com 40 ambientes assinados por um elenco de 52 profissionais da arquitetura, design de interiores e paisagismo.

Texturas, aromas, iluminação indireta, arte, música, vegetação, materiais naturais e peças autorais aparecem como ferramentas para provocar emoções e pertencimento, sem deixar de lado a tecnologia.

Além da mostra, quatro operações gastronômicas estão montadas na CASACOR, seguindo a mesma narrativa dos demais ambientes.

O restaurante Aroma, comandado pelo chef Ronny Peterson e projetado pelo Studio Roque Arquitetura de Rômulo Carvalho, propõe uma experiência inspirada na ancestralidade e na cultura negra.

A cafeteria Entre Fluxos, operada pela Lilie Pâtisserie & Boulangerie, transforma uma pausa para o café em um momento de encontro, com projeto do escritório Bruno Carvalho Arquitetura.

Já o Bar Ocelo, que ocupa o ambiente desenvolvido por Orestes Blanco e Rosa Maranini, recria a atmosfera dos speakeasies da década de 1920, a partir de um projeto inspirado na fusão latino-oriental.

A operação é do CO/RE, nascido da parceria entre Fernando Zeta, bartender que construiu sua trajetória em São Paulo e Goiânia, e o chef Yago Ferreira (A Casa do Porco), com passagens pelas edições da CASACOR Goiânia.

Ambiente CASACOR Brasília 2026 — Foto: Divulgação

Um projeto para unificar a arquitetura e as experiência dos rótulos premiados da vinícola goiana São Patrício, que podem ser degustados em taças ou em garrafas. O projeto é assinado por Eliene Lucindo do Laboratório de Interiores.

O espaço criado por Aline Silva e Amanda Beatriz abriga a chocolateria LaBarr. A marca que trabalha com cacau cultivado por pequenos produtores brasileiros conta com um espaço que representa o processo produtivo do chocolate.

A sustentabilidade está incorporada ao planejamento da mostra. Com uma gestão centralizada dos resíduos, o evento busca alcançar 99,7% de valorização dos materiais – índice necessário para a conquista da certificação Lixo Zero – com reaproveitamento e destinação de materiais a organizações sociais.

Em diversos ambientes, sustentabilidade e arquitetura caminham juntas. Arquitetos e designers propõem soluções como o uso de construção seca, madeiras certificadas, materiais recicláveis, aço produzido em economia circular, reaproveitamento de pedras naturais e telhas de demolição, revestimentos de baixo impacto ambiental, iluminação em LED e pisos ecológicos.

A valorização do paisagismo nativo também reforça esse compromisso. Diversos ambientes privilegiam espécies do Cerrado, reduzindo o consumo de água e fortalecendo a identidade regional.

Em outros espaços, mobiliário produzido por artesãos brasileiros, peças de design autoral e materiais reaproveitados demonstram a união entre sofisticação e responsabilidade ambiental.

Outro compromisso sustentável da mostra é o desenvolvimento de ambientes com 100% de acessibilidade, garantindo uma experiência inclusiva em toda a extensão da mostra.

articles.summary: Almost every front page on Monday is dominated by the what the Telegraph suggests is an "Iran link" to a "bomb plot" at RAF Fairford.
articles.body:
Many of the front pages feature a photograph of what the Daily Mail describes as five "shirtless terror suspects" as they were being arrested near RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire.

The Daily Telegraph says counter-terrorism police are investigating whether Iran was behind a suspected bomb plot at the base, while the Daily Star notes that the US flew bombing raids against Iran from Fairford.

The Sun says it's chilling that "a massive terror attack" was thwarted by the quick thinking of a "hero farmer," who spotted the suspects on the way back from a party.

The Times says the pensions "triple lock" could be axed to fund free social care for elderly people in England. The i Paper believes Andy Burnham has signalled that major tax hikes could be required to pay for his new National Care Service.

The Sun says it will mean "another raid on the pay packets or savings of millions of hard-working families, already being squeezed from every direction." The Daily Express says the prime minister has recognised the urgent need to address one of the greatest policy failures of modern times - but adds that we should all be fearful after he admitted "nothing is off the table."

The Guardian describes the stand-off between unionists and nationalists in Portadown as a "ghost from the past," saying the decision to allow an Orange Order parade down the Garvaghy Road has ignited old tensions. The Daily Mail agrees that the tense stand-off threatens to return Northern Ireland to its embittered past.

The Daily Mirror says Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy has told a panel at the Labour conference that tech firms could be exempt from the social media ban for under-16s if they innovate to make their platforms safe. The paper says she told the panel it would be up to the companies to act if they wanted to get themselves off the banned list.

It reports five men have been arrested for "terror and explosive offences" after three suspicious vans were reported travelling towards RAF Fairford. Counter terrorism police are now leading the investigation into the incident at the base, according to the paper. It says that in July, Iran threatened to attack the base, on the basis that anywhere used to launch strikes on Iran was a "legitimate target". articles.title: Powerful nor’easter floods US Northeast, leaves over 100,000 without power
articles.summary: A powerful nor’easter continued to batter the US Northeast on Sunday, bringing coastal flooding, strong winds and dangerous surf from New Jersey to New
articles.body: A powerful nor’easter continued to batter the US Northeast on Sunday, bringing coastal flooding, strong winds and dangerous surf from New Jersey to New England, while disrupting power supplies and air travel across the region.According news agency AP, the storm killed a New York City Housing Authority worker on Saturday after a falling tree struck the worker. More than 100,000 customers across the Northeast and mid-Atlantic were without power at various points, while coastal communities faced repeated flooding as the slow-moving storm lingered over the region.New Jersey was among the worst-hit areas, with low-lying coastal communities experiencing repeated flooding during successive high tides. Some parts of the state received more than 4 inches of rain since Friday, adding to the flood threat.In Sea Bright, a coastal community in New Jersey, residents and businesses dealt with rising water as another high tide brought fresh flooding. Officials warned that additional tidal flooding could occur as the storm continued to move slowly through the region.The storm also brought strong winds to parts of New York. On Long Island, trees and utility poles were knocked down, causing power outages and damaging property.The National Weather Service said the storm was expected to weaken, but warned that the threat from coastal flooding would continue. Another round of high tides could bring further flooding to parts of New Jersey and New York.The weather system also disrupted air travel. More than 250 flights were cancelled at Boston Logan International Airport by late Sunday morning, while wind gusts at the airport reached around 40 mph.In New York City, several inches of water covered streets in the Howard Beach neighbourhood. Other coastal communities across the Northeast also reported flooding as strong winds pushed seawater inland.The storm has revived memories of Superstorm Sandy, which devastated parts of the US east coast in 2012 and caused more than $60 billion in damage. However, the current nor’easter is not comparable to Sandy in terms of overall impact, AP reported.Residents in some New Jersey communities said measures introduced after Sandy, including raising homes and using sandbags, helped limit damage from the latest storm.The nor’easter could also be the first of several major storms to affect the US east coast this fall, with meteorologists pointing to the influence of an El Niño weather pattern.You use AI every day. articles.title: "I began reading a lot and this shaped my life": He lost most of his eyesight at 8, grew up with an autorickshaw-driver father; how Ajay R Raj cracked UPSC with AIR 109
articles.summary: At around eight years old, Ajay R Raj lost most of his eyesight.
articles.body: At around eight years old, Ajay R Raj lost most of his eyesight.For a child growing up in a small town in Kerala's Western Ghats, between Kozhikode and Wayanad, it could have narrowed the world considerably. His family, too, was not one of privilege. His father was an autorickshaw driver and his mother a homemaker. Meeting household expenses while funding their son's education was a struggle.But somewhere between the financial limitations at home and the gradual loss of his eyesight, Raj found something that gave him access to a much larger world: books. In Class 5, he discovered a small library in his town. For the boy from the countryside with partial visual impairment, it became much more than a place to borrow books.“Coming from the countryside and due to my partial visual impairment, the library and the books were my sole window to the outside world,” Raj wrote in a first-person account published by YourStory in 2022. “I read voraciously on different works of literature and it started shaping my life,” he wrote.It was around this time that another dream took shape. “Since fifth grade, it was my dream to be able to study at St. Stephen’s College, Delhi,” he recalled in the YourStory account.Years later, Raj would not only make it to St Stephen's College but go on to pursue postgraduate studies in English literature, teach at a college and repeatedly sit for one of India's toughest competitive examinations.In March 2026, after five attempts, he secured All India Rank 109 in the UPSC Civil Services Examination, moving significantly up from his earlier rank of 730. But the rank is perhaps the easiest part of his story to tell. The harder part began when he was still a child.When his eyesight began to fadeAccording to The Economic Times, Raj's eyesight deteriorated when he was around eight or nine, leaving him unable to see clearly and eventually causing him to lose most of his eyesight. The report also notes that his father, an autorickshaw driver, supported the family and his son's education despite financial difficulty.For Raj, education was not something he took for granted. It was something he actively fought to hold on to. After Class 10, his desire to learn pushed him to leave his hometown for the city. But another obstacle was waiting. He had studied in a Malayalam-medium school and was trying to enter the CBSE system.“I was utterly shattered when I learnt that the new school was wary about admitting a Malayalam medium school educated boy into the CBSE stream,” Raj wrote. “They tried to dissuade me from joining, but that didn’t deter me.”The transition was difficult. He was away from home, adjusting to hostel life and the pressures of a new city while simultaneously trying to prove himself academically. His answer was to study. “Right after school, I used to run back to the hostel and immerse myself in studies,” he wrote.He went from being one among the top 10 students to becoming the topper. By Class 12, he had topped the Humanities stream and set a new record at his school. He also secured the first rank nationally in the PwD category and eighth in the general category, according to his account. The boy who had once found a window to the world in a small library was now preparing to walk through a much bigger door.From a small Kerala town to St Stephen'sRaj eventually reached St Stephen's College in Delhi, the institution he had dreamed about since Class 5. College brought a different set of challenges. He was studying literature, a subject he loved, but his visual impairment made reading and comprehending texts difficult.“Although I was passionate about literature, I had to encounter N number of difficulties in comprehending the texts, internalising the logic of literature,” he wrote. This time, however, he did not face those difficulties alone. “With the help of my friends, I surmounted such hurdles and became the university rank holder in the PWD category,” Raj wrote.His academic journey took him beyond the classroom. He wrote about the exposure he received at St Stephen's, including an internship with Harvard University and qualifying for the first round of the Rhodes Scholarship to the University of Oxford.Yet, somewhere along the way, his ambitions moved beyond his own education. “My interest in public service- both as a beneficiary and as an agent of change--inspired me to pursue civil service,” he wrote. He also described his motivation as a desire to contribute to the society that had shaped him. The dream was now the UPSC.The examination that refused to be conquered easilyThe civil services examination did not yield immediately.Raj's journey included attempts where he could not clear the preliminary stage and others where he fell short at the mains stage, according to The Economic Times. Financial pressure also meant that preparation could not always be his only occupation. He worked as an English teacher and taught cultural studies at a college while continuing his UPSC preparation.The setbacks accumulated, but so did the experience. Eventually, Raj secured AIR 730 in the UPSC examination and was selected for the Railway Service. For someone who had grown up watching his father work as an autorickshaw driver to support the family, a government service was already a significant achievement.But Raj had another destination in mind. He chose to attempt the civil services examination again. And again. And again.By the time he appeared for his fifth attempt, he had already experienced both failure and success. He had cleared the examination once. He had a service in hand. Yet he was still not ready to let go of his IAS dream. “This was my fifth attempt and my third serious one,” Raj told the media after securing AIR 109, as reported by The Times of India.His approach to UPSC had also evolved. “I viewed UPSC preparation not merely as a test, but as a journey for skill development,” he said. “Even if one doesn't make it, the skills gained would be invaluable elsewhere,” Raj added. That mindset perhaps explains why the earlier result did not become the end of his story.AIR 109, but the journey started much earlierIn the latest examination, Raj jumped from his earlier AIR 730 to AIR 109. The result put him closer to the IAS dream he had continued to pursue even after entering the Railway Service. He has credited his family, academic mentors and the preparation ecosystem at LEAD IAS Academy in Thiruvananthapuram for supporting him through the journey.“My preparation was built around the mechanism developed by the academy, bolstered by constant support of my seniors and juniors,” he previously told The Times of India. But long before coaching centres and civil services preparation became part of his life, there was a small library in Kerala.There was a boy who could not see the world clearly but found a way to explore it through literature. There was a father driving an autorickshaw and trying, despite financial difficulties, to keep his son's education going. There was a child who moved away from home, struggled to adapt to a new school and refused to accept that coming from a Malayalam-medium background should decide what he could become.There were difficult books, supportive friends, academic achievements, unsuccessful UPSC attempts and, eventually, a first selection that still did not feel like the final destination. Looking back at his journey in his 2022 YourStory account, Raj had already articulated what education meant to him.“For any vulnerable section, education is the best tool for upward mobility,” he wrote. And then came a line that now reads almost like a promise he made to himself: “I know my journey is not over yet. Destinations are still remaining with the support of the organisation.” Four years later, his AIR 109 result is another milestone in that journey. For Raj, the story was never simply about clearing an examination despite impaired vision.It began much earlier- with a family that had limited means, a father whose work was behind the wheel of an autorickshaw, a child whose eyesight was fading, and a small library that gave him a way to see beyond all of it.The books did not restore his eyesight. They did something else. They gave him a vision of where he could go.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ testGet the latest Lifestyle News and more. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: At 21°C, Delhi records its lowest minimum temperature in Sept in 18 years
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Delhi’s Sunday recorded its lowest minimum temperature in 18 years — 21 degrees Celsius, three notches below normal.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Delhi’s Sunday recorded its lowest minimum temperature in 18 years — 21 degrees Celsius, three notches below normal.With cool north and north-easterly winds, heavy rain and storm in adjoining states and large parts of northern, central and eastern India, Delhi has been experiencing early winter-like mornings.However, Met expects both minimum and maximum temperatures to gradually rise over the next few days.“The minimum temperature of 21 degrees Celsius recorded at Safdarjung was the second-lowest minimum temperature recorded in the month of Sept since 2001. The lowest was 20.8 degrees Celsius, recorded on Sept 6, 2008, and the third lowest was 21.1 degrees Celsius, on Sept 19, 2024,” said Krishna Mishra, weather scientist at IMD.While Ridge recorded a minimum of 16.8 degrees Celsius, Palam saw 19.2 degrees Celsius and Ayanagar 21.2 degrees Celsius. On Saturday, the minimum temperature was 23.2 degrees Celsius.At base station Safdarjung, the maximum temperature was recorded at 30.6 degrees Celsius, four notches below normal, against 29.2 degrees Celsius a day earlier.As ‘good’ as it gets: Parts of capital soak in air benefits of Sept showersThe city also saw its air quality improve within the ‘satisfactory’ category. The AQI at 4pm Sunday was 53 — the best air quality Delhi has seen since July 9, when it stood at 48. In many parts, the air quality was recorded in the ‘good’ category.On Monday, the minimum temperature is expected in the 20-22 degrees range while the maximum is likely to hover around 31-33 degrees Celsius. As per Met, no showers are expected from Monday onwards.Met said very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall was recorded due to a deep depression formation over the west-central bay – from Andra Pradesh to Odisha, Chhattisgarh, eastern Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand, Bihar, UP till Uttarakhand.“A very large area saw intense rain activity, up to more than 30cm at many places in UP. The low minimum temperatures in Delhi and adjoining areas can be attributed to this large-scale rain,” Mishra said, adding that minimum temperature departures in UP, Chhattisgarh and eastern MP are running up to 4 degrees below normal.“The maximum temperature departure on Sunday was up to 10 degrees below normal in parts of UP; 5-7 degrees below normal in parts of Chhattisgarh and MP; and 7-8 degrees below normal in Uttarakhand. Even in Delhi, it was around four notches below normal in some parts,” he said, adding that the weather will soon turn dry, with monsoon withdrawal advancing to parts of UP and Punjab, and beyond.While Delhi saw monsoon retreat on Sept 23, two days before its normal withdrawal, with 728.6mm of rainfall (Safdarjung), which is considered normal and 16% above the average monsoon rainfall of 629.7mm, parts of the city recorded 5mm post-monsoon rainfall Saturday due to the depression and western disturbance feeding additional moisture in the region.Last year, the city recorded 41% surplus rainfall.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news.
